function: Pilot (PDSCH DM-RS) time-domain allocation for the next downlink slot, chosen from uplink CSI with implicit UL-to-DL channel prediction to maximize throughput without CSI feedback (p. 2).
system: Single-user downlink massive MIMO-OFDM, FDD; BS 8×8 array, UE 2×1 array; no RIS; NR band n1 (UL 1.95 GHz, DL 2.14 GHz), 100 MHz bandwidth (pp. 2, 4).
method: ViViT (spatial and temporal transformer encoders, MLP softmax head) or 3D-CNN classifier over 13 DM-RS patterns; supervised on exhaustive-search optimal-allocation labels (pp. 2-4).
data_channel: Ray-traced channels from NVIDIA Sionna RT on its simple_street_canyon_with_cars scene, UE in a car at 60-80 km/h; 6,000 slots (4,000 noise-augmented), split 8:1:1 (p. 4).
test_conditions: Training and test slots from the same scene and speeds (8:1:1 split); tests sweep SNR −10 to 15 dB and QPSK to 256-QAM over 250 slots (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: CNN-based DQN [24]; disjoint ViViT/CNN channel predictor [22] plus DM-RS pruning [23]. Non-learned: minimum DM-RS (maximize data symbols), random allocation; exhaustive-search optimum as upper bound (p. 4).
metrics: Classification accuracy of the optimal DM-RS allocation index per SNR; average data throughput versus SNR for QPSK to 256-QAM; NMSE reported for the disjoint predictor only (pp. 4-5).
complexity: ViViT O(L(N²D+ND²)), about 1.082×10⁹ FLOPs, about 3.47 µs on an NVIDIA A100 computed from peak FLOP rate; CNN O(LFCK³HWT), fewer FLOPs (pp. 3-4).
q1_support: p. 4: "We utilized the ray-tracing module of NVIDIA Sionna to generate channel data"; p. 4: "We employed the simple_street_canyon_with_cars scene" (public Sionna RT scene, not a listed model; reviewer to confirm, see notes).
q2_support: p. 4: "the dataset was split into training/validation/test sets with an 8:1:1 ratio" (one scene and one speed range, 60-80 km/h; tests vary only SNR and modulation; no unseen scenario, configuration, or site).
q3_support: p. 4: "DRL [24]: A CNN-based deep Q-network"; p. 4: "Maximize Data Symbols: A heuristic scheme that maximizes the number of transmitted data symbols"; p. 5: "Average data throughput achieved by each scheme’s DM-RS allocation".
q4_support: p. 3: "The ViViT complexity is O(L(N²D + ND²))"; p. 4: "the ViViT model requires ∼1.082 × 10⁹ FLOPs".
q5_support: p. 4: "We utilized the ray-tracing module of NVIDIA Sionna to generate channel data" (own generated channels, not released; no code or data link, availability statement, or public channel dataset anywhere in the paper).
notes: PDF is arXiv 2507.11064v2; its title and authors match the Crossref record of the DOI (IEEE TVT, 2026). Eligibility borderline on function: the network outputs a DM-RS (pilot) time pattern, not a channel estimate, and channel prediction is implicit (p. 2: 'directly classifies the optimal allocation'). I read it as pilot allocation for channel estimation and CSI-feedback reduction, area 2 (pp. 1-2); if the reviewer takes adaptive DM-RS selection as link adaptation, the code would be function. q1: channels come from Sionna RT ray tracing on the public built-in scene simple_street_canyon_with_cars (p. 4), not one of the listed models; marked met for the reviewer to confirm as a public ray-tracing source. q5 stays 0 even if q1 is confirmed, since the generated channels (placement, trajectories, Gaussian augmentation) are neither released nor fully specified. q3: DQN [24] is a standard algorithm applied to the same problem; the disjoint baseline combines published learned methods [22], [23] with the CPRS backbone settings. CPRS (CNN) is a second backbone of the proposed method, not a baseline. q4: the 3.47 µs is computed from FLOPs and the A100 peak rate, not measured.
